entries:
Literally, “in front of oneself along”.
Until the earlier 19th century the prepositions für (“for”) and vor (“before”) were not distinguished strictly. In this idiom particularly, it may be questioned which of the two is the more proper interpretation. Vor does make good enough sense with verbs such as vor sich hin singen (“to sing to oneself”), but on the whole für may actually be considered more appropriate. Irrespective of this, only vor is now standard and has generally established itself.
senses: to/for oneself (alone, not directed at anyone else)
slowly but steadily, without being bothered or interrupted by anyone
